summary: Intermittent burst latency and uneven GPU slot distribution in dedicated pool (bank imbalance)
description:
Issue summary: Multiple StratusDocs tenants in a single dedicated reservation are experiencing intermittent 3–7x request latency spikes during short (30s–2m) burst windows. The spikes correlate to reduced per-GPU throughput despite aggregate GPU utilization being below reservation limits.

Impact: Customer-facing inference endpoints return high tail latencies, causing degraded UX for chat workloads and several user timeouts; revenue impact for StratusDocs is material during peak traffic.

Environment: Dedicated reservation ID dr-78f9 in us-east with 8xA100 nodes, RBAC-policed, autoscaling disabled for the reservation. Affected routes are pinned to redwood-open-vicuna-13b and llama-2-13b-chat.

Observed behavior: During bursts of concurrent short requests (avg tokens per request ~60, 95th concurrency bursts to 120), certain GPUs in the pool show sustained KV cache thrashing and per-slot queue backpressure while sibling GPUs idle or show low scheduling. Autoscaler remains inert (disabled) but the scheduler’s bin-packing appears to favor a subset of slots, creating a temporary ‘bank imbalance’ in allocations.

Expected behavior: Incoming requests should be relatively evenly distributed across GPUs in the reservation; per-GPU KV cache and batch sizing should prevent localized backpressure and avoid 5xx/timeouts for bursty short requests.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use a short-concurrency burst generator (internal tool: perf-burst) aimed at reservation dr-78f9.
2) Send 120 concurrent short requests (payload ~60 tokens) to the pinned route redwood-open-vicuna-13b for 90 seconds.
3) Observe per-GPU token throughput and request latencies via /console -> Dedicated -> dr-78f9 -> Metrics.
4) Repeat with different routing policies (spread vs. binpack) and record variance.
observed_behavior: Tail P95/P99 latency spikes to 1200–2200ms; request-level 429s not observed but timeouts increase by ~8% during windows. Telemetry shows GPU0/1/2 receiving >60% of new KV cache warmups and heavy kernel contention while GPUs 3–7 have 10–20% fewer inflight tokens. Node-level GPU utilization appears 55–70% overall, masking per-device hotspots.
expected_behavior: Even distribution of load across GPUs in the reservation. Lower P95/P99 (target < 400ms) and negligible timeout rate for same workload.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: scheduler bin-packing heuristics + request burst pattern cause allocation hot-spotting on contiguous GPU indices leading to cache churn.
What we checked: scheduler logs, per-GPU kernel queues, KV cache miss rates, inter-GPU balance metrics.
Findings so far:
- Binpack scoring favors lower-index devices under current scoring weights for memory locality.
- KV cache prewarm currently insufficient for short-burst workloads; misses concentrated on GPUs handling new allocations.
- Autoscaler disabled so no capacity expansion; there is available capacity on sibling GPUs that isn't used because of allocation heuristics.
- Similar pattern reproduced locally with perf-burst when scheduler policy set to binpack.
Hypothesis: For bursty short requests, binpack increases cache warmups concentrated on a subset of devices; combined with per-device kernel queue limits this produces transient throughput collapse.
Next steps: test 'spread' allocation policy in a controlled window for customer; instrument a temporary scheduler metric to surface imbalance index; consider short-term mitigation to rotate initial allocation indices to better distribute warmups.
comments: Maya Chen (Customer): Noticed the issue first on Monday morning. It affects our corporate chat flow and causes customer complaints. We need a workaround while you investigate.
Ethan Wallace (Support): Thanks — we’ve started capturing per-GPU metrics and confirmed a bank imbalance pattern. Working on repro. Will propose a mitigation in 2 hours.
Priya Kapoor (SRE): Reproduced locally with perf-burst. Binpack policy reproduces the hot-spot. Spread policy removes the extreme tail but increases average inter-GPU memory churn slightly.
Jamal Ortiz (Eng - Scheduler): Added a temporary logging patch to surface allocation distribution and imbalance_index to telemetry. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2241
Ethan Wallace (Support): Customer consented to a 20-minute controlled test switching routing to 'spread' policy at 2026-03-12T16:00Z.
resolution:
Workaround applied: temporarily switched reservation routing policy from 'binpack' to 'spread' for dr-78f9 at 2026-03-12T16:05Z; this reduced P99 from ~2200ms to ~420ms for the observed workload window.
Longer-term action items: 1) Scheduler change to incorporate 'kv_cache_warmup_penalty' into binpack scoring (ENG-#2241). 2) Add imbalance_index and per-reservation auto-rotation of allocation anchors for short-burst detection. 3) Add guidance to Dedicated docs for customers with bursty short-token workloads recommending spread or mixed policies.
Status: Mitigation successful; follow-up engineering tasks opened. Customer notified and monitoring in place.
